1	## OfficeFloor REST endpoints
2	
3	Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
4	OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
5	pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.
6	
7	- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
8	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
9	  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
10	  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
11	- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
12	  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
13	- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
14	- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
15	- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
16	- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.
17	
18	### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
19	
20	The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
21	
22	`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
23	
24	```yaml
25	# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
26	# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
27	validate:
28	  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
29	  next: load
30	load:
31	  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
32	  next: apply
33	apply:
34	  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
35	  govern: [ transaction ]
36	  next: save
37	save:
38	  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
39	  govern: [ transaction ]
40	  next: respond
41	respond:
42	  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
43	```
44	
45	```java
46	// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
47	public class ValidateOwner {
48	  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
49	    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
50	  }
51	}
52	public class LoadOwner {
53	  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
54	      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
55	    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
56	    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
57	    ownerOut.set(owner);
58	  }
59	}
60	public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
61	  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
62	    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
63	    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
64	  }
65	}
66	public class SaveOwner {
67	  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
68	    repository.save(owner);
69	  }
70	}
71	public class RespondWithOwner {
72	  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
73	    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
74	  }
75	}
76	```
77	
78	`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
79	
80	```yaml
81	handle:
82	  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
83	```
84	
85	```java
86	public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
87	  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
88	      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
89	    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
90	  }
91	}
92	```
93	
94	### Step wiring
95	
96	Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
97	point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
98	method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
99	`method:`.
100	
101	- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
102	  as `@Parameter T`.
103	- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
104	  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
105	  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
106	
107	### Function parameters
108	
109	Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
110	
111	- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
112	- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
113	- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
114	  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
115	  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
116	- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
117	  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
118	
119	### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
120	
121	Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
122	into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
123	
124	- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
125	- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
126	  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
127	- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
128	  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
129	
130	### Naming
131	
132	Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
133	absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
134	publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
135	`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
136	
137	Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
138	responder. Steps in between work with entities.
139	
140	### Request body and validation
141	
142	- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
143	  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
144	  first step publishes it as a variable.
145	- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
146	  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
147	  invalid body can return 400.
148	
149	### Transactions
150	
151	`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
152	listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
153	the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
154	
155	### Errors
156	
157	Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
158	Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
159	`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
160	`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
161	anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
162	
163	### Security
164	
165	Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
166	
167	```yaml
168	composition:
169	  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
170	```
171	
172	- Full reference: https://officefloor.net/llms.txt

	}

```

`LoadOwner`, `SaveOwner`, `DeleteOwner`, `BuildOwner`, `ApplyOwner`, `ValidateOwner`, `ListOwners`, `ListOwnersPage`, `RespondWithOwner`, `RespondWithOwnerCreated`, `RespondWithOwnerUpdated`, `AuditOwnerCreated(Event)`, `CheckCityCapacity`, `FlagCapacityWarning`, `CheckEmailDomain`, `FlagPossibleDuplicate`, `CheckUniqueIdentity`, `CheckUniqueEmail`, `CheckUniqueTelephone`, `CheckUniqueHousehold`, `DeduplicateCustomerCode`, `Soundex`, `IdempotencyStore`, `OwnerSegment`, plus (from POST YAML) `CheckIdempotencyKey`, `AssignHouseholdId`, `ValidatePostcode`, `AdjustRegistrationDate`, `CheckDailyLimit`, `AssignCustomerCode`, `AssignNamesakeCount`, `FlagBulkSignup`, `RecordIdempotencyKey`, `NotifyWelcome`, `MembershipLevel`, `HouseholdCeiling`, `FiscalYear`, `Locality`, `Timezone`, `AgeBand`, `TelephoneDisplay`.

- `Collection<Owner> findByLastName(String)` / `Page<Owner> findByLastName(String, Pageable)`
- `Owner findById(int)`

- `void delete(Owner)`

**Maven** (wrapper `./mvnw`; `pom.xml` present, artifact `spring-petclinic-rest`, Spring Boot starter parent). No Gradle. DTOs generated via `openapi-generator` plugin; JaCoCo and Surefire present. ```

```
To run just the acceptance test:
```

```
Docs: `readme.md` shows `./mvnw spring-boot:run`; `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` document the OfficeFloor endpoint conventions (no explicit test command given).

---

### 8. Config/properties for capacity / disposable domains / risk

There is **no externalized configuration** for these — all thresholds and lists are **hard-coded constants in Java**:
- Disposable domains: inline `Set.of(...)` in `CheckEmailDomain.java`.
- City capacity: `CAPACITY = 50` in `CheckCityCapacity.java`; `WARN_THRESHOLD = 40` in `FlagCapacityWarning.java`.
- No `risk`/`capacity`/`disposable` keys in any `application*.properties` or `messages*.properties`.

`application*.properties` files exist (`application.properties`, `application-h2/hsqldb/mysql/postgres.properties`) but contain only datasource/JPA/OfficeFloor config, nothing risk-related.

---

### Practical implications for implementing `riskFlag`
1. Add a `riskFlag` `readOnly: true` boolean under `Owner` in `openapi.yml` (~line 2249) so `OwnerDto` gains the field.
2. Add a `@Mapping(target = "riskFlag", expression = "java(...)")` to `OwnerMapper.toOwnerDto` combining the three conditions. Inputs available directly on the entity: `owner.isPossibleDuplicate()`, city-over-soft-capacity (compute via `OwnerRepository` + `CheckCityCapacity.normalize`, mirroring `FlagCapacityWarning`), and disposable-adjacent email (extend/adapt `CheckEmailDomain`'s blocklist logic).
3. Because the test reads `riskFlag` back through `GET /api/owners/{id}` → `RespondWithOwner` → `toOwnerDto`, computing it in the mapper (rather than only a POST-time transient flag) is the safest single-point approach. If instead you store it as a transient on `Owner` set during POST, note the GET path reloads a fresh entity from the repository, so transient POST-time state would be lost — the mapper/repository must recompute on read.

  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type

        status:

          format: int32

          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true

          title: Detail

          type: string

          readOnly: true

          title: Timestamp

          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: Optional honorific (MR/MRS/MS/DR). When present it prefixes the salutation.
          type: string
          example: DR
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. On write, accepted for
            backward-compatibility when the structured addressLine1 is absent. On
            read, the composed normalized address (addressLine1, plus a space and
            addressLine2 when present).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the structured postal address. Preferred over the flat
            'address' when present; an owner is valid with either a non-blank
            addressLine1 or the flat address, plus a city.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: The optional second line of the structured postal address.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: The email address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'

          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'

          writeOnly: true
          example: false
        postcode:
          title: Postcode

    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.

              readOnly: true
            displayName:

              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: The title and last name ('DR Who'), or just the last name when no title is given.
              type: string
              example: 'DR Who'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone (display)
              description: The stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans - country code, a space, then the national digits grouped in threes. Raw 'telephone' stays E.164.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            memberId:
              title: Member ID
              description: "Unified member identifier '<REGION><FY><HASH8><CHK>': the region code, the 2-digit fiscal year of the registration date, the first eight upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over telephone + lastName, and a single Luhn check digit over the digits of the preceding segments."
              type: string
              example: 'NSW263F5A1B9C4'
              readOnly: true
            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: "'FY<YY>' for the fiscal year (starting 1 July) of the business-day-adjusted registrationDate, named for the calendar year it ends in."
              type: string
              example: 'FY26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: Stable identifier shared by owners at the same lastName and address who opted in with sharesHousehold. Absent otherwise.
              type: string
              example: 'a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: "Derived duplicate key: normalizedTelephone + '|' + (email or empty) + '|' + householdId. Two owners are duplicates only when their whole identityKey matches."
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: Number of existing owners sharing the same firstName and lastName (case-insensitively) at the moment this owner was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: "Membership points: +2 when an email is present, +1 when namesakeCount is 0, +2 for a household of three or more, +3 for tenure over 365 days."
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: "Numeric membership level derived from membershipPoints: 1 (0-1 points), 2 (2-3), 3 (4-5), 4 (6 or more)."
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: "Region derived from city via a fixed table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' for any other city."
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            ownerSegment:
              title: Owner segment
              description: "Segment as '<TIER>_<AREA>': TIER is 'PREMIUM' at membershipLevel 3 or more else 'STANDARD'; AREA is 'METRO' for a known region (NSW/VIC/QLD) else 'REGIONAL'."
              type: string
              example: 'STANDARD_METRO'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: "IANA timezone derived from the locality/region via a fixed table (NSW->Australia/Sydney, VIC->Australia/Melbourne, QLD->Australia/Brisbane). Absent for any other region."
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: "'EMAIL' when the owner has an email, otherwise 'PHONE'."
              type: string
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: "Derived from birthDate against registrationDate: 'MINOR' (under 18), 'ADULT' (18-64) or 'SENIOR' (65+). Absent when birthDate is omitted."
              type: string
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:

              description: True when more than 80 owners had already been created today at the moment this owner was created, otherwise false.

              example: false
              readOnly: true
            capacityWarning:

              description: True when the owner's city already held 40-49 owners (approaching the hard limit of 50) at the moment this owner was created, otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicate:

              example: false
              readOnly: true

              format: int32

              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
